reasons: Status is correctly classified as a deviation: Section 13 is mutual and therefore binds the Customer, contrary to the preferred position of no non-solicit on us, while already sitting close to the fallback (mutual, one year, limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services, solicitation-only).

The redline is the smallest edit that reaches the fallback: it appends a carve-out sentence for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches (including hiring those who respond) without deleting or rewriting the operative language, and no no-hire language exists to strike.

The failed 'duration ≤ 12 months' check is a phrasing artifact — the clause says 'one (1) year', which satisfies the 12-month fallback and is well inside the 24-month walk-away — and the high changed-character ratio simply reflects the length of the appended carve-out relative to a short clause, not an unnecessary rewrite.

The comment accurately describes what changed, cites the playbook position (no non-solicit on Customer) and states the acceptable fallback in the required concise, first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.

Minor residual point the drafter could have flagged: the one-year tail runs from termination of the Agreement rather than from the end of the individual's involvement, but this is within the fallback tolerance and does not invalidate the edit.
